newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle market slow at $72- feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle market slow at $72- feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains cattle markets were slow Friday, with a small number of cattle trading in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma, feedlot sources said.
About 100 head sold at $72.00 per cwt, steady with Thursday, and $2.00 above last week's top, the sources said.
Most feedlots sold out their showlists this week and were expected to have smaller numbers of finished cattle available next week, which could strengthen prices further.
Cattle next week were expected to be priced at $74.00, with bids seen at $72.00, but trades could be be light until the end of next week because of this week's big sales.
USDA estimated this week's sales in the Panhandle at a record large 196,000 head, above the previous record of 155,400 set the week ended Aug 22 this year.
Sales in Kansas were pegged at 125,700 head, hefty but below the weekly record of 136,400 set this summer the week of Aug 22.

Demand this week was generated by strong boxed beef prices, with some packers buying cattle a week beyond the normal seven-day delivery period to ensure they had inventory to fill beef orders, sources said.
